subject: Operational smoke tests + SLO deep-dive (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)
messages:
From: Tim Holloway <tim.holloway@cloudcorp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudCorp SRE Team <sre@cloudcorp.com>
Date: 2027-01-25T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reliability questions + next tests

Priya — thanks for the demo today. Quick notes from our side after the call: we liked Redwood's deterministic routing and the dedicated-pool option, but we need to be thorough on operational behavior before a procurement recommendation. The questions we need answers for are primarily around: uptime guarantees and consequences, rate-limiting behavior for bursty traffic, error-budget handling and automatic failover.

Specific asks: 
- Can you share a concise SLO comparison (Redwood hosted vs Cloud Hyperscale endpoints) for uptime, p95/p99 latency under 100/500/1k RPS, and documented rate limits?
- What observable signals trigger automatic fallback to a smaller model or a different region? How does KV/prefix cache interact with failover (do we warm caches or fall back cold)?
- We'd like a short operational test plan we can run with our SREs that covers: sustained QPS, cold-start/kv-cache eviction, mid-run instance failure injection, and rate-limit throttling.

I'm looping in our SREs; can Redwood propose owners and a schedule for the tests next week?

Thanks,
Tim Holloway
Senior Platform Architect
CloudCorp

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Tim Holloway <tim.holloway@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-27T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: reliability questions + next tests

Tim — really appreciate the clear checklist. Summary and proposal below (TL;DR at top + proposed owners/schedule).

TL;DR: We'll provide a 1-page SLO comparison, an operational smoke-test plan (PDF), and a three-day test window runbook. Redwood will own test orchestration and failure injection; CloudCorp SRE runs the orchestrated client load from your side. Proposed test window: Feb 2-4 (flexible).

High level answers to your bullets:
- SLO comparison (attached spreadsheet): Redwood hosted: target uptime 99.95% (SLA for Dedicated customers can be 99.95–99.99% depending on contract), typical p95/p99 under production-like load for our backbone models: p95 ~ 45–120ms, p99 ~ 200–420ms (varies by model size and sequence length). Hyperscaler managed endpoints we've benchmarked: baseline uptime often 99.9% for shared endpoints; p99s vary and tail latencies can be higher under autoscale churn. I've put conservative numbers in the attached redwood-slo-comparison.xlsx so you have a side-by-side.

- Rate limits & burst handling: hosted API enforces soft token-based rate limits per API key (we publish token/sec and hard burst limits). For Dedicated customers you get predictable capacity and configurable burst policies. If traffic exceeds capacity, Redwood will return 429s with a retry-after header; for critical tiers we support automatic priority preemption and failover to a warm standby model variant (smaller quantized model) to conserve tokens while maintaining availability. Exact token/sec numbers depend on model and reserved capacity — we'll include a profile in the spreadsheet.

- Failover & cache behavior: automatic fallback is triggered by health checks and sustained error rates (default threshold: 5% error rate over 1 minute or sustained P99 > configured SLO for 3 minutes). When failing over to a smaller model we fall back cold (KV cache isn't portable across model variants), but we will warm critical prefixes by replaying recent requests from the routing proxy when configured (this is an opt-in behavior during the test run). Cache warming times depend on prefix diversity; we'll show expected warm-up curves during the test.

Operational smoke-test plan (attached failure-injection-plan.pdf) — short version:
1) Sustained QPS ramp: run 100 -> 1k RPS for 30m stages to observe autoscaling, P95/P99, error rates.
2) Cold cache run: restart serving nodes and run representative prompt set to measure cold-start latencies and KV cache impact.
3) Failure injection: kill 1/3 of replicas mid-stage and observe route failover, error budget burn, and fallback effectiveness to quantized variant.
4) Rate-limit test: hit token-based limits from a set of client IPs to validate 429 behavior, retry-after semantics, and client-side backoff.

Proposed owners & schedule:
- Redwood orchestration and monitoring: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.com) — test harness, failure injection scripts, and metric dashboards.
- Redwood runtime tuning & failover policy lead: Rishi Malhotra (rishi@redwood.com) — will tune thresholds and oversee cache-warm logic.
- CloudCorp SRE: Tim Holloway + SRE Team — run client load generators from your VPC, provide network conditions, and validate from your observability.

Next steps and asks from CloudCorp before we run:
- Confirm a 3-day window (we proposed Feb 2-4) and a contact for on-call coordination.
- Share a representative prompt set and target sequence lengths so we can match traffic profiles.
- If you prefer a Dedicated evaluation (predictable capacity), let us know target QPS and model family to generate a dedicated-pool quote.

I've attached the short spreadsheet and the failure-injection plan. Ben and Rishi are on-copied and will follow up with a lightweight runbook and dashboard links tomorrow.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m prep call if useful.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com

Priya — adding a couple of technical clarifications and proposed metric checkpoints to include in the dashboard (so CloudCorp SREs know what to watch):

On Fri, Jan 27, 2027 at 10:15 AM Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com> wrote:
> TL;DR: We'll provide a 1-page SLO comparison, an operational smoke-test plan (PDF), and a three-day test window runbook. Redwood will own test orchestration and failure injection; CloudCorp SRE runs the orchestrated client load from your side. Proposed test window: Feb 2-4 (flexible).

Proposed additional checkpoints to the plan:
- Health-check signals: CPU/GPU utilization, pod restarts, queue depth (requests waiting for batch), per-instance token/sec throughput.
- Error categories: 5xx internal errors, 4xx client errors (e.g., malformed requests), and 429 throttles — capture both counts and rolling percentages.
- Error budget math: expose a 30-day error budget for the test tenant; compute burn rate and simulate a corkscrew scenario where bursts drive a simulated gradual burn so we validate automated throttles and notifications.
- Tail-latency observation: capture p90/p95/p99 by model variant and by region. For failover tests also capture cold-start latency distribution (first 100 requests post-failover).

Test automation notes: our failure injection will use graceful drain first, then forced kill to simulate different RTOs. For the model-variant fallback, we will provide a mocked small-quantized model in the Dedicated pool to avoid cross-variance cache assumptions.

I'll prepare the metric list and a Grafana link (read-only) before Feb 1 so CloudCorp can pre-add dashboards. Also recommending a short prep call on Feb 1 to go through runbook toggles (cache-warm on/off, fallback thresholds).

—Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
